This issue is not a duplicate of the two mentioned.

#18615 is about the model parameter being ignored when launching a subagent by agent name (it falls back to the agent's built-in chain). In my case, the subagents are correctly using the models I configured. I can confirm this with opencode stats --models, where I see messages and tokens being consumed on Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.4, Gemini 3.1 Pro, etc.
#16937 is about the Desktop App consuming separate premium requests per subagent (higher total usage). My issue is different: it's about billing attribution.

Actual problem:
Even though OpenCode internally executes the subagents with their configured cheaper models, all Premium Requests (300 in my case) are being billed by GitHub Copilot exclusively to the orchestrator's model (Claude Opus 4.6). In the GitHub Copilot usage CSV, the other models show 0 requests.

In short:

Model selection works correctly at runtime.
Billing attribution fails with the GitHub Copilot provider: everything is charged to the expensive main agent model.

Can this be reviewed by the team? It appears there is an issue with how the model is passed to the GitHub Copilot API when using subagents in "subagent" mode.

> Hi @kitlangton, noticed this PR is still in draft — wanted to flag a related timing issue we've been investigating that might be worth considering as part of this refactor. We traced a bug (#20026) where plugin providers registered via the config() hook disappear after /instance/dispose. The root cause is that configProviders = Object.entries(cfg.provider ?? {}) is captured as a stale snapshot before plugin.list() runs and calls the config() hook. When plugins modify cfg.provider to add their providers, it's already too late. Your refactor injects dep (with auth and config bridges) into custom loaders, which is a nice improvement — but it doesn't address the ordering of plugin.list() relative to configProviders. Since this PR is still in draft, would you be open to proposing a solution that also addresses the initialization ordering? We have a fix in PR #20777 that moves plugin.list() to run before configProviders, but we'd be happy to see a more elegant approach from you if you think it fits better into this refactor. Happy to collaborate or adjust our approach if you have ideas.
